executiveSummary.headline: Correct Core Meeting Facts Before Pursuing Broader Visibility
executiveSummary.lead: Wyndham San Diego Bayside leads its five-hotel Wyndham Rewards peer set, but absolute consideration remains low at 13.6%, with presence in only 34.8% of eligible scenarios. The peer rank is encouraging context, not evidence of strong overall visibility.
executiveSummary.metricsNote: These metrics describe presence in monitored AI answers—not bookings, revenue, or traveler exposure.

themes.title: Meeting Facts Need Immediate Repair
themes.what: The homepage displays meeting-stat labels without values, while two Hotel schema graphs conflict on check-in and checkout times and one states 27,000 square feet of meeting space.
themes.whyItMatters: Planners and automated systems need one approved set of basic facts; visible blanks and conflicting machine-readable details reduce confidence.

themes.title: The Meetings Story Has a Usable Base
themes.what: A dedicated meetings page already presents commercial meetings and weddings content, so the task is alignment rather than inventing a new proposition.
themes.whyItMatters: Matching the homepage, meetings page, and structured data gives sales teams and prospective planners a consistent, credible official account of capacity and fit.

themes.title: Access and Competitive Gaps Need Diagnosis
themes.what: A Node probe received Cloudflare 403 responses although browser-based tools could read the site; ADP also noted Hotel del Coronado displacement.
themes.whyItMatters: Neither observation establishes a site outage or competitive cause, so both require bounded, documented technical partner investigation before security changes or public positioning claims.

priorities.action: Repair homepage facts and Hotel schema
priorities.desiredOutcome: One accurate guest and planner fact set

priorities.action: Align meetings facts across official pages

executiveSummary.successLooksLike: Homepage meeting figures, operational times, meetings copy, and structured data agree with a hotel-signed source of truth; technical and competitor questions have documented decisions.
executiveSummary.closing: Executive Takeaway: Wyndham San Diego Bayside should treat its peer lead as a starting point, not a victory lap. Fix the visible and machine-readable fact conflicts first, then decide whether technical access or sharper bayside and meetings differentiation merits further investment.

actions.headline: Investigate Cloudflare Access for Intended Crawlers
actions.priorityWhy: A bounded Node probe received 403 responses, but browser-based retrieval worked.
actions.whatWeFound: Automated Node requests to the homepage and robots target received Cloudflare 403 responses, while browser and WebFetch access succeeded. This is not proof of a public outage or universal crawler block.
actions.whyItMatters: The agency should establish whether intended search and AI crawlers receive official content before changing security rules. Investigation protects both accessibility and site security.
recommendedSteps: Open a Cloudflare review with timestamps and user agents.
Confirm the intended robots policy from an approved environment.
Compare WAF behavior for intended crawlers and ordinary automation.
Retest after any hotel-approved rule change.
actions.timeframeNote: Timing is proposed and requires accountable-owner agreement.

completionCriteria.investigationCompleted: A reproducible access matrix documents client, region, URL, status, and expected policy.
completionCriteria.correctionSubmitted: If a mismatch is confirmed, a hotel-approved Cloudflare ticket identifies the narrow rule adjustment.
completionCriteria.correctionVerifiedLive: Agreed clients successfully retest named URLs, or expected denials are documented with rationale.
completionCriteria.noChangeRequired: Valid if the security partner confirms intended crawlers are served and the Node result is environment-specific; decision memo is filed.

actions.hotelApprovalNotes: Do not alter WAF or bot-management rules without hotel and security-partner approval.

changesOrInvestigation: Inspect Cloudflare event logs for the probe window.
Compare observed treatment with intended crawler policy.
Prefer a narrow rule change only if a mismatch is confirmed.
technicalDetails.verificationMethod: Security-partner ticket plus before-and-after access matrix from agreed test clients.
dependencies: Do not alter WAF or bot-management rules without hotel and security-partner approval.
technicalDetails.notes: The 403 is an investigation signal, not a requirement to change CDN or security configuration.
